about.ru: Припев песни Рэя Хендерсона (1926) по первому изданию. Тональность соль мажор.
about.en: The chorus of Ray Henderson's 1926 song from the first edition. Key of G major.

source: Ray Henderson / Mort Dixon, Bye Bye Blackbird, Jerome H. Remick & Co., New York / Detroit, 1926, first edition, 'Operatic Edition' with ukulele arrangement, Earl and Bell cover (IMSLP #873484), chorus, vocal line and ukulele chord symbols; public domain
notes: Source pages: chorus = PDF pages 4–5 (printed pages 4 and 5), cut time (¢) read as 4 quarters = 8 eighths per bar; every bar checked to sum to 8 eighths (rests fill the gaps).

Chord placement: the uke diagrams in bars 2, 3, 4, 10, 11, 26, 27 put the second chord over the SECOND quarter note (beat 2), not beat 3. Our format splits a two-chord bar at beat 3, so 'C G', 'Bm D7', 'Am7 G', 'D Am', 'D7 Bm' sound the second chord one beat later than printed. In bars 21, 22, 28, 30, 31 the second chord is printed on beat 3 and matches the format.

Bar 17: the edition prints G7 on beat 1, Bb (uke diagram) over the 4th quarter note, then G7 again on bar 18. A Bb on beat 4 alone cannot be expressed (two chords split at beat 3), so bar 17 is just 'G7'; the Bb passing chord is dropped.

Bars 6 and 20: printed '(C#-7)' and '(G#-7)'; the 1920s '-7' sign read as a diminished seventh -> 'C#dim7', 'G#dim7' (from the period convention and harmonic function: G - C#dim - Am7 D7; Dm - G#dim - Am). The uke diagrams were not decoded fret by fret to confirm.

Chords not printed in a bar carry over the last printed chord: bar 5 = G (from bar 4), bar 8 = D7, bars 13–14 = D7, bar 16 = G, bar 30 beats 1–2 = Am (printed D7 on beat 3), bar 32 = G (printed over its first note).
Symbols kept as printed: 'G', 'C', 'D', 'Bm', 'Am', 'Cm', 'Dm' (plain triads, no 6 or 7 added), 'Am7', 'D7', 'G7', 'A7', 'E7'. No augmented chords occur in the chorus (the G+5 is only in the verse).

Ties (bar 7->8 F#4, 15->16 G4, 29->30 C5, 31->32 G4) are encoded as a new event at t 0 of the next bar with "tie": true. The app's melodyBarNotes()/melodyNotes()/melodyExercise() skip tie events, so a tied note is not struck again.

Bar 32 (2nd ending): half G4 tied (curved line, same pitch) to a quarter G4, then a quarter rest; written as one G4 of 6 eighths. Lyric 'Bye___' is one held syllable, so the curve is read as a tie, not a slur to a re-struck note.

Bar 22: C5 B4 A4 G4 quarters ('sto-ries they all'). A small dot below the stem of B4 and a small mark above the last note (G4) look like print specks, not a dotted rhythm or accidental; read as plain quarters.
Bar 28: A4, G#4 (printed sharp), then half note on the same line read as G#4 because the sharp carries through the bar (no natural printed).

1st ending (not used; bars 31–32 here are the 2nd ending): bar 31 = G4 half + half rest, chords G (beat 1) Em (beat 3), lyric 'Bye'; bar 32 = whole rest, chords E7 (beat 1), A7 (beat 3), D7 (beat 4), then repeat to the start of the chorus. The 2nd ending prints G (bar 31 beat 1), C (bar 31 beat 3), G (bar 32).
Bar 29–30: half A4, half C5 tied to a quarter C5 in bar 30, quarter rest, half F#4 ('Bye') under D7.

Lyric text is from the same page (verse 1 only on the chorus: 'Pack up all my care and woe...'). Notes were read from crops of the full-resolution page renders (about 4150 px wide, higher than 300 dpi); no bar was filled from memory, all pitches were placed by staff position.
